goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers to inspect a page as repository content, distinguish nodes from properties, use the Sling Resource mental model, and classify content, configuration and code by repository boundary.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 3 of a seven-week AEM Sites training course, delivered Wednesday, August 19, 2026. The audience is learning traditional AEM Sites on AEM as a Cloud Service through WKND. This class focuses on JCR hierarchy, page anatomy, Sling Resources, and the responsibilities of /content, /conf and /apps. A supplied repository snapshot can replace a live environment.
deck_context.core_claim: An AEM page becomes easier to reason about when every observation is tied to a path, a node or property, and the repository boundary that owns its lifecycle.

sample_generation_method.input_context_preparation: Use view_image to inspect the approved sample PNG before generation, then pass it to image_gen as a style-only reference.
sample_generation_method.handoff_rule: Subagents must use the same built-in image_gen backend in generate mode and return a blocker if unavailable.

style.name: Detailed AEM repository atlas
style.visual_direction: Information-rich technical blueprint blended with sober academic courseware. Each slide must contain credible AEM paths, node or property labels, precise annotations and meaningful connectors rather than generic corporate cards.
style.color_palette: Warm off-white drafting-paper background; deep navy typography; faint square grid; semantic blue for authored content, green for configuration, violet for application code and restrained slate for neutral repository concepts.
style.typography: Crisp modern sans serif headings and labels; true monospace appearance for paths, node names, properties and types; strong hierarchy readable on a projected slide.
style.texture_and_finish: Flat 2D technical drawing with fine rules, restrained colored headers, precise tree glyphs and subtle drafting-grid texture. No gradients, neon, glass, 3D icons or photography.
style.deck_consistency: Match the approved sample's palette, typography, annotation density, line weight, grid texture and AEM-specific technical precision while varying composition by slide role.

approved_style_reference.fidelity: Match style, palette, typography, density and technical precision only; do not copy the exact three-boundary layout.

slides.title: Read AEM as a resource tree.
slides.intent: Open the session with the inspection path from an authored page to repository content, configuration and rendering code.
key_points: Class 3 · Week 1 · Day 3 · August 19, 2026
JCR, resources and repository boundaries
From an authored page to the code that renders it
Juan Maldonado

local_context.required_background: The observable outcome is to inspect an AEM page, distinguish nodes from properties, and explain whether an item belongs to /content, /conf or /apps.

layout.composition: Editorial cover with a large repository tree growing from one browser page card and branching toward /content, /conf and /apps.

constraints: Render the date and class metadata exactly.
Keep the cover visually rich but text sparse.

slides.title: JCR stores a hierarchy, not a table of pages.
slides.intent: Replace file-folder and relational-table assumptions with the addressable repository-tree mental model.
key_points: A repository is an addressable tree
Nodes create structure and paths
Properties store values on nodes
Node types describe intended shape and behavior

local_context.required_background: Use a credible WKND path and identify the path, nodes, properties and node types without implying that JCR is merely a filesystem.

layout.composition: Large annotated repository tree on the left, compact comparison against a relational row on the right, with the tree clearly presented as the AEM model.

visual_elements.main_visual: A /content/wknd/us/en/guide tree whose branches are labeled node and whose attached values are labeled property.

constraints: Use node, property, path and node type precisely.
Do not call nodes folders or properties files.

slides.title: A node holds structure; properties hold values.
slides.intent: Give learners precise inspection vocabulary for nodes, child nodes, scalar values, multi-value properties and primary types.
key_points: Child nodes represent nested structure
Properties can be scalar or multi-value
jcr:primaryType identifies the node's primary type
A path identifies a node; a property name identifies a value on it

local_context.required_background: Show a repository inspector close-up for /content/wknd/us/en/guide/jcr:content with example properties jcr:title, sling:resourceType and cq:tags.

layout.composition: Repository inspector close-up split into a left hierarchy pane and a right property table with numbered callouts.

visual_elements.main_visual: Selected jcr:content node with child nodes below it and a property grid containing names, types and example values.

constraints: Render jcr:primaryType, jcr:title, sling:resourceType and cq:tags exactly.
Clearly distinguish a multi-value property from child nodes.

slides.title: One page has two important layers.
slides.intent: Connect the Sites console page to its cq:Page container, jcr:content content resource and component descendants.
key_points: The page container is commonly a cq:Page node
jcr:content stores authored content and metadata
Component instances appear below jcr:content
The browser URL and repository path are related but different views

local_context.required_background: Use a Guide Page example. Show /content/wknd/us/en/guide as cq:Page and /content/wknd/us/en/guide/jcr:content as cq:PageContent, with a root/container component descendant.

layout.composition: Exploded page anatomy: Sites console card at left, repository layers at center and component descendant tree at right.

visual_elements.main_visual: A two-layer page section with cq:Page above jcr:content, plus a separate browser URL label.

constraints: Do not state that the cq:Page node itself stores all authored component values.
Keep cq:PageContent as an example node type for jcr:content.

slides.title: Sling exposes repository content as resources.
slides.intent: Translate repository storage into the application-facing Sling Resource model used by AEM code.
key_points: A Sling Resource has a path, properties and children
ValueMap provides a convenient view of properties
sling:resourceType connects content to rendering capability
Prefer the Resource API unless the requirement is specifically JCR-level

local_context.required_background: JCR is a persistence model; Sling Resource is the application abstraction. Avoid claiming they are identical. Use /content/wknd/us/en/guide/jcr:content/root/container/guide as the example resource.

layout.composition: Translation pipeline from JCR node view to Sling Resource card to component capability, with a ValueMap inset.

visual_elements.main_visual: A repository node transformed into a resource card containing path, children, ValueMap and sling:resourceType.

constraints: Do not equate a JCR Node object with a Sling Resource object.

slides.title: Content, configuration and code have different owners.
slides.intent: Distinguish /content, /conf and /apps by ownership, mutability and deployment lifecycle.
key_points: /content: what authors manage
/conf: how the site is configured
/apps: how the application works
Different paths. Different owners. Different lifecycles.

slides.title: Trace one Guide Page without changing it.
slides.intent: Apply the mental model through an evidence chain that works from a supplied snapshot or an optional local Author instance.
key_points: Start at /content/wknd/us/en/guide
Inspect jcr:content and authored properties
Read sling:resourceType
Locate the matching component under /apps
Identify the related template or policy under /conf

slides.title: Key takeaways
slides.intent: Consolidate the four mental models before questions.
key_points: AEM content is an addressable hierarchy of nodes and properties
cq:Page and jcr:content describe different parts of a page
Sling Resources are the application-facing view of repository content
/content, /conf and /apps separate authored content, configuration and code
